question: Explain the distinction between the three broad types of majority vote requirements outlined in the report.
answer: Majority of votes cast refers to a "simple majority" where more than half of the votes cast must be in favor; Majority of all members means at least half plus one of the total legislators must vote in favor, whether present or not; Supermajority requirements signify a need for more than a simple or absolute majority, also known as a "qualified" or "special" majority.
